extracted.intended_audience: independent inventors and small businesses filing patent applications without legal representation (pro se applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for independent (pro se) inventors and small businesses on preparing and filing patent applications with the USPTO, including required parts of an application, applicable application types, patentability standards, pre‑filing searches, amendment procedures, and procedural reminders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Se Assistance Program outreach and educational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pro Se Assistance Program supports independent inventors and small businesses filing patent applications without legal representation. The program provides outreach and educational resources to help "pro se" applicants—those filing independently—make informed decisions and improve application quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the program's outreach and educational materials to learn filing procedures, common pitfalls, and resources available before and during prosecution. Seek program resources to improve application quality and understanding of USPTO processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Filing Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, pro se applicants need: Specification (detailed written description of the invention); Claims (defining the scope of protection sought); Drawings (when necessary for understanding); Abstract and title of the invention; Appropriate filing fees (varying by application type); Executed Oath or Declaration (establishing inventorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all listed parts are prepared and included at filing. Verify appropriate filing fees for the specific application type. Completeness and correct execution (e.g., oath/declaration) are common areas where pro se applicants make errors—review USPTO guidance before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application types and their purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility Patents: For new, useful processes, machines, manufactures, or compositions of matter. Design Patents: For new, original ornamental designs for articles of manufacture. Plant Patents: For new plant varieties that are asexually reproduced. Provisional Applications: Placeholder applications establishing early filing dates (not examined; must file nonprovisional within 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the application type that matches the invention and filing strategy. Note that provisonals are not examined and do not grant patent rights—use them only to secure an early filing date before filing a nonprovisional application within 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical patentability requirements (utility patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility patents, inventions must be: New: Not identically disclosed in prior art. Non-obvious: Meaningfully different from existing technology. Useful: Accomplishes something with "specific, substantial, and credible" utility. Cannot be patented: Laws of nature, abstract ideas, mere ideas without complete description, or literary/artistic works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting the specification and claims, address novelty, non-obviousness, and the specific, substantial, and credible utility of the invention. Avoid claiming ineligible subject matter (laws of nature, abstract ideas, etc.) and ensure the disclosure is complete enough to support the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing recommendation: conduct a prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a prior art search to determine whether similar inventions already exist. The USPTO provides: Public Search Facility in Alexandria, Virginia; Patent and Trademark Resource Centers at libraries nationwide; Web-based tutorials and search strategy guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use USPTO facilities and tutorials to perform searches before filing to assess novelty and patentability, refine claim scope, and reduce the likelihood of avoidable rejections. A prior art search is recommended to inform drafting and filing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment process guidance for specifications, claims, and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For specifications: Submit marked-up copies showing additions (underlined) and deletions (struck through), plus clean versions. For claims: Indicate status of each claim—Original, Currently amended, New, Canceled, etc. For drawings: Submit replacement sheets labeled clearly, explaining all changes in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amending, follow USPTO formatting and labeling conventions to clearly show changes and maintain clean copies. Properly categorize claim status to aid examiner review. Clearly explain drawing replacements to avoid confusion during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important procedural reminders and prosecution options
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent pending protection only applies after filing—provisional applications provide "no actual patent protection." Pro se applicants frequently make errors on forms; the USPTO emphasizes reviewing guidance materials and seeking assistance before submitting applications. The Patent Trial and Appeal Board handles appeals if examiners reject applications, and inventors can request interviews with examiners during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that filing creates 'patent pending' status but provisional filings do not grant enforceable patent rights. Double-check forms to avoid common errors. If an application is rejected, consider examiner interviews and PTAB appeal options; use available USPTO resources or assistance programs when needed.
